title: TCP-based sources: idle connections starve busy connections (`RequestLimiter` capped at `num_threads()`)

type.name: Bug
type.description: An unexpected problem or behavior

body:
### A note for the community

<!-- Please keep this note for the community -->
* Please vote on this issue by adding a 👍 [reaction](https://blog.github.com/2016-03-10-add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/) to the original issue to help the community and maintainers prioritize this request
* If you are interested in working on this issue or have submitted a pull request, please leave a comment
<!-- Thank you for keeping this note for the community -->

### Problem

All sources built on `TcpSource` (`socket`, `syslog`, `fluent`, `logstash`, `statsd`) use one `RequestLimiter` per source. Its number of permits is capped at `crate::num_threads()`, the number of available CPUs:

https://github.com/vectordotdev/vector/blob/e44fb91fa1ce822b8ce45d66ea925e497431e6d9/src/sources/util/net/tcp/mod.rs#L171-L172

A connection must hold a permit before it reads. It keeps the permit:

- for up to 10 ms while it waits for data (added in #11549):
  https://github.com/vectordotdev/vector/blob/e44fb91fa1ce822b8ce45d66ea925e497431e6d9/src/sources/util/net/tcp/mod.rs#L360-L374
- while it is blocked in `send_batch`, and until delivery when `acknowledgements` is enabled:
  https://github.com/vectordotdev/vector/blob/e44fb91fa1ce822b8ce45d66ea925e497431e6d9/src/sources/util/net/tcp/mod.rs#L422-L434

The semaphore is FIFO, and each turn reads at most one `ReadyFrames` batch (1024 frames). So one round takes about `connections × hold time / permits`. When many connections are quiet, a busy connection gets a turn only every few hundred ms. Its kernel receive queue fills and the sender sees a zero window, while Vector's CPU usage stays low and the downstream buffers stay empty.

Expected: the throughput of a busy connection should not depend on how many idle connections are open.

This is the same problem as #23392, which #23448 fixed for `dnstap` only.

### Configuration

```yaml
sources:
  src:
    type: socket
    mode: tcp
    address: 127.0.0.1:7010
    decoding:
      codec: bytes
    framing:
      method: octet_counting
sinks:
  out:
    type: blackhole
    inputs: [src]
    print_interval_secs: 0
```

For the last row of the results, add a second identical source on port 7011 and send the busy connection there.

### Version

vector 0.58.0 (aarch64-apple-darwin 2bcad9b 2026-08-26 13:37:07.557544670)

### Example Data

On a 16-CPU machine (16 permits): one connection sends ~100 B octet-counted frames as fast as it can, and N other connections are open.

| Other connections | Busy connection |
|---|---|
| 0 | 55 MiB/s |
| 8 | 56 MiB/s |
| 16 | 28 MiB/s |
| 64 idle | 2.3 MiB/s |
| 256 idle | 0.66 MiB/s |
| 750 idle | 0.06–0.37 MiB/s |
| 750, each sends one frame every 100 ms | 1.2 MiB/s |
| 750, each sends one frame every 10 ms | 5.3 MiB/s |
| 750 idle, busy connection on a separate source | 52 MiB/s |

Vector CPU was ~100% with no other connections (one connection uses one core) and ~7% in a run with 750 idle connections (that run also had a `route` transform).

The measurements match the model: 256 idle × 10 ms / 16 permits = 160 ms per round, so at most 1024 frames per 160 ms ≈ 6.4k events/s. The measured value was 6.8k events/s.

<details>
<summary>Load generator</summary>

Usage: `python3 load.py <other_connections> <other_interval_secs, 0 = idle> <duration_secs> [busy_port]`

```python
import resource, socket, sys, threading, time

resource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_NOFILE, (8192, 8192))

ADDR = ("127.0.0.1", 7010)
N_OTHER = int(sys.argv[1])
OTHER_INTERVAL = float(sys.argv[2])
DURATION = float(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 10.0

body = b"date=2026-09-18 time=13:17:40 devname=fgt01 type=traffic subtype=forward srcip=10.0.0.1 act=accept"
frame = str(len(body)).encode() + b" " + body
chunk = frame * (1_048_576 // len(frame))

stop = threading.Event()
others = [socket.create_connection(ADDR) for _ in range(N_OTHER)]

def trickle(s):
    while not stop.is_set():
        try:
            s.sendall(frame)
        except OSError:
            return
        stop.wait(OTHER_INTERVAL)

if OTHER_INTERVAL > 0:
    for s in others:
        threading.Thread(target=trickle, args=(s,), daemon=True).start()

time.sleep(1.0)
busy = socket.create_connection((ADDR[0], int(sys.argv[4]) if len(sys.argv) > 4 else ADDR[1]))
sent = 0
start = time.monotonic()
while time.monotonic() - start < DURATION:
    busy.sendall(chunk)
    sent += len(chunk)
elapsed = time.monotonic() - start
stop.set()
print(f"others={N_OTHER} busy={sent / elapsed / 1_048_576:.2f} MiB/s")
```

</details>

### Additional Context

We cannot simply copy the #23448 fix (raise the cap). In `dnstap` a permit covers one event, and a setting (`max_frame_handling_tasks`) already existed. In `TcpSource` a permit covers a whole batch: up to 1024 frames, or a full `fluent` request. The CPU cap comes from the backpressure RFC ("A value higher than this has no benefit, but would use more memory"). That assumption holds only if a connection holds a permit while it does CPU work, not while it waits.

If we raise the cap, the RFC's other limit (100k events divided by the average batch size) must bound memory. With mixed traffic, many 1-event batches keep the average low, so the permit count goes up to the cap. Under backpressure, each permit keeps its decoded batch in memory. The worst case goes from `num_threads × 1024` to `cap × 1024` events.

Options to explore:

1. **Take a permit only when data is ready.** Wait until the socket is readable, then acquire the permit. This keeps the RFC's memory bound. The wait must be skipped when `FramedRead` or the TLS layer already has buffered bytes, or the connection can stall.
2. **Raise the cap behind a new option**, like `max_frame_handling_tasks` for `dnstap`. This is a simple change, but memory use under backpressure grows as described above.
3. **Shorten the 10 ms idle timeout.** This reduces the effect but does not remove it, and it adds wakeups for every idle connection.

Workaround: put the busy senders on a separate source (port). Each source has its own limit.

### References

- Discussion #26430
- #23392, #23448 (same problem, fixed for `dnstap`)
- #11549 (10 ms idle timeout)
- #10962 and `rfcs/2022-01-06-8596-tcp-source-backpressure.md` (request limiter design)

**Errors like:**
- "Failed to publish events caused by: read tcp XXX.XX.XXX.XX:XXXX->XXX.XX.XXX.XX:XXXX: i/o timeout"
- "Failed to publish events caused by: write tcp XXX.XX.XXX.XX:XXXX->XXX.XX.XXX.XX:XXXX: use of closed network connection"

- "Failed to publish events caused by: EOF filesdf"
- "File cleanup state update error: input outlet closed"
- "Failed to publish events caused by: invalid sequence number received (seq=1024, expected=6)"

**Some of the things we noticed:**
- With an increase of these errors, we are seeing duplicate logs, we suspect it's because filebeat resends them because either Vector didn't ack or didn't ack in time.
- Not seeing any utilization issues, infact utilization is low. Checked cpu, memory, file descriptor limit, network i/o, storage i/o, etc.
- **Important:** Restarting the Vector services gets rid of the errors for a couple days, then it resurfaces after it's been running for some days.

Any ideas on what we could check? Could there be some internal limit in Vector that we're hitting?

title: Logstash source can attempt to decompress nested compressed frames, aka zipbomb/DoS

type.name: Bug
type.description: An unexpected problem or behavior

body:
### A note for the community

<!-- Please keep this note for the community -->
* Please vote on this issue by adding a 👍 [reaction](https://blog.github.com/2016-03-10-add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/) to the original issue to help the community and maintainers prioritize this request
* If you are interested in working on this issue or have submitted a pull request, please leave a comment
<!-- Thank you for keeping this note for the community -->


### Problem

I may be misunderstanding this but i don't see any guard code. Looking at src/sources/logstash.rs - when a LogstashFrameType::Compressed frame is decompressed, decode() is called on the output buffer without any indication/hint that it's going to be operating on decompressed data. That next run though decode() on the decompressed buffer could happily read/decompress more compressed frames, which themselves could contain compressed frames, and so on. Nesting compressed frames in such manner is a very low-bandwidth way to blow up memory usage and crash daemons via malicious traffic.

Simplest fix would be adding a boolean when instantiating LogstashDecoder, to indicate whether it's been created to decode raw data or compressed data. So make the struct:

```
struct LogstashDecoder {
    state: LogstashDecoderReadState,
    inside_compressed_frame: bool,
}
```

And have LogstashDecoder::new() accept a bool argument setting inside_compressed_frame. it would be set false in normal initialization, and only set to true for the decoder that's created inside the LogstashFrameType::Compressed match in the decode() loop. Then in the LogstashFrameType::Compressed match, check the bool and skip any compressed frames when we're operating over decompressed data.

The integration tests for the `fluent` and `logstash` sources set up their own containers for the relevant servers to run the tests, which they then delete at the end of the tests. This is different from the other integration tests which are managed with standardized start/stop scripts. This setup has a few potential problems;
1. Test failures during development can result in extraneous containers left running.
2. The tests are hard-coded to use a docker socket API, making interoperability with podman difficult.
3. Problems with setting up the containers can masquerade as test failures.

If possible, these tests should be reworked to use the standard start/stop setup.

title: Propagate backpressure by not accepting new connections for TCP-based sources

type.name: Enhancement
type.description: Improvement or extension to something that already exists.

body:
We observed in https://github.com/timberio/vector/issues/8238 that, in the presence of back-pressure, Vector does not stop accepting new TCP connections for TCP-based sources. Instead it accepts them and deserializes the first "message" from the wire, blocking when it attempts to push to the next components (`Pipeline.send`). This will cause it to hold open connections and memory.

Similar to https://github.com/timberio/vector/issues/7186 I think we should have a configurable ceiling after which Vector will refuse to accept additional connections while it processes those in-flight.

## How to reproduce

### Prepare a pod vector + filebeat

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: vector-test
spec:
  containers:
    - name: vector
      command: [sleep]
      args: [infinity]
      image: timberio/vector:0.27.0-debian
      resources:
        limits:
          cpu: "1000m"  #  NO ISSUE IF SET TO 2000m
          memory: 512Mi
        requests:
          cpu: "250m"
          memory: 256Mi

    - name: filebeat
      command: [sleep]
      args: [infinity]
      image: docker.elastic.co/beats/filebeat:8.5.1
```

### Start Vector

```shell
kubectl exec -it vector- -c vector -- bash

rm /etc/vector/vector.toml

cat > /etc/vector/main.yml <<EOF
    sources:
      my_input:
        type: logstash
        address: 0.0.0.0:5044
    sinks:
      my_sink:
        type: file
        inputs: [my_input]
        encoding:
          codec: json
        path: /tmp/vector-%Y-%m-%d.log
EOF

export RUST_BACKTRACE=full
vector --config-dir /etc/vector/
```

### Start Filebeat

```shell
kubectl exec -it vector-test -c filebeat -- bash

bash -c "while true; do date --utc >> /tmp/test.log; sleep 5; done" &

cat > /tmp/filebeat.yml <<EOF
filebeat.inputs:
  - type: log
    paths: [/tmp/test.log]

output.logstash:
  hosts: "localhost"

logging:
  json: true
  level: "debug"
EOF

filebeat -e -E http.enabled=true -c /tmp/filebeat.yml
```

### Additional Context

This happens on Kubernetes when Vector container is set with `resources.limit.cpu: 1000m`, (while no issue for 2000m).

- other 0.27.0 images (alpine, distroless) have the same issue
- Vector version 0.26.0 have no issue

### Use Cases

Vector is a useful source solution to feed to a Logstash environment, being far more efficient than a single instance of Logstash, and easy to deploy. We can't avoid using Logstash pipelines on the backend at the moment, but we can scale them horizontally, allowing us to increase throughput.

Vector doesn't support the ndjson format in the HTTP sink that Logstash is expecting, and while we could recursively process the ndjson in the Logstash environment, this isn't how we'd deploy it in production nor is it useful for benchmarking a Logstash pipeline. 

Vector is transmitting the HTTP format in an a JSON array. Logstash's HTTP input expects it to be a slightly awkward ndjson, and it ends each line with a comma and then a \n.

Additional use cases would be simply naive Vector collectors passing to a Logstash HTTP receiver. As noted in https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/logstash/current/ls-to-ls.html the advice is stick with HTTP to HTTP if reliability can be answered. This is particularly relevant in the MSP style situation where we don't have full control of the logging endpoint, and some transform of data is required before loading into a data lake.



### Attempted Solutions

We tried various codecs and mime type applications in Logstash, but none worked to unwrap the log data properly.

I did look at the source to see if I could implement a PR for this, but my knowledge of Rust is minimal and while I could follow the code I didn't think I could rapidly solve the problem.

StephenW on Discord responded to my query and suggested I write up a feature request.

### Proposal

Extend Vector's http sink to support both ndjson and Logstash ndjson as an encoding method.

title: Memory leak when merge is used

type.name: Bug
type.description: An unexpected problem or behavior

body:
### Vector Version

```
$ vector -V  
vector 0.14.0 (x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu 5f3a319 2021-06-03)
```

### Vector Configuration File

```toml
[sources.logstash_logs]
type = "http"
address = "0.0.0.0:1234"
encoding = "json"

# Route logs for parsing based on tags.
[transforms.parse_routes]
type = "route"
inputs = ["logstash_logs"]
route."http_logs" = 'includes!(.tags, "http_logs")==true'

[transforms.format_http_logs]
type = "remap" 
inputs = ["parse_routes.http_logs"] 
source = '''

# Store logstash metadata.
meta._hostname = .host."name"
meta._host_ip = .beat."hostname"
meta._source = .source

# Parse all the extra query params in the HTTP body and merge with
# above metadata.
http_extra_params = parse_query_string!(.http_extra_params)
params = merge(http_extra_params,meta)
http_body = encode_json(params)

# Prepare the full event payload.
. = {
    "http_body": http_body,
}
'''

[sinks.blackhole]
type = "blackhole"
inputs = ["format_http_logs"]
```


### Expected Behavior

No memory leak should happen.

### Actual Behavior

Memory leak happens as seen in the below graph

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5689132/123136365-7a681800-d470-11eb-8c4b-a263133e9232.png)


### Additional Context

I split the config into different parts and after eliminating each part of the config, I found the memory leak happens because of:

```
params = merge(http_extra_params,meta)
```

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5689132/123136697-d92d9180-d470-11eb-910b-c37ccd9bae29.png)

If I don't have this `merge`, there's no memory leak. In the above graph:

1: Added `merge()`
2:  Removed `merge()`

As soon as this `merge` is introduced, memory starts to leak.

- Baseline when I just have the `input.http` and `sink.blackhole` is ~700MB.
- When I add the above transformation without `merge` it hovers around ~700-900MB.
- When I add `merge(http_extra_params,meta)` memory keeps on increasing until OOM killed.

- So far it looks like `.params = merge(http_extra_params,meta)` and `.params = {"http_extra_params": http_extra_params, "meta": .meta}` both are culprits for increasing memory. So this in fact could be something to do with the payload? There's a `parse_query_string` in the above line which might be involved in this too.

- Interestingly `del(.params)` didn't have an effect on reducing the memory.


Happy to provide additional details if required.

body:
We should consider application level message acknowledgement with the `vector` source and sink. This ensures data is not dropped. Logstash, for example, has created the [lumberjack protocol](https://github.com/elastic/logstash-forwarder/blob/master/PROTOCOL.md) for this purpose. It might make sense to adopt that protocol since we'll need it for https://github.com/timberio/vector/issues/420.

A couple of questions:

* What kind of performance impact will this have?
* Where do we draw the line on durability before recommending a system designed for this purpose (ex: kinesis / kafka)?

Broken off of: https://github.com/timberio/vector/pull/4779

title: windows_event_log: source does not re-subscribe on ERROR_EVT_QUERY_RESULT_STALE (0x80073AA3) and gets stuck in a pull loop on high-volume channels

type.name: Bug
type.description: An unexpected problem or behavior

body:
### A note for the community

<!-- Please keep this note for the community -->
* Please vote on this issue by adding a 👍 [reaction](https://blog.github.com/2016-03-10-add-reactions-to-pull-requests-issues-and-comments/) to the original issue to help the community and maintainers prioritize this request
* If you are interested in working on this issue or have submitted a pull request, please leave a comment
<!-- Thank you for keeping this note for the community -->


### Problem

## Summary
On a high-volume Windows channel — the Security log on a Domain Controller — the `windows_event_log` source stops ingesting after the log rolls over and never recovers on its own. A pull returns `ERROR_EVT_QUERY_RESULT_STALE` (0x80073AA3); the source then logs "Recoverable pull error, backing off." and retries the **same, now-invalid** subscription with exponential backoff (100 ms doubling, capped at 5 s) — one failed pull every 5 s, indefinitely. It resumes only after a process restart. On an unattended fleet this presents as recurring multi-hour gaps in Security data.

This is specific to `ERROR_EVT_QUERY_RESULT_STALE`. The sibling error `ERROR_EVT_QUERY_RESULT_INVALID_POSITION` is already handled correctly (it re-subscribes), which is what makes the fix small and low-risk.

## The same error, two code paths — one recovers, one does not
The same STALE error is handled in two places with opposite outcomes, and the **Security channel alone shows both** in one 0.57.0 run (verbatim logs in Debug Output):
- **At SUBSCRIBE (process start) → RECOVERS.** The open path retries without the bookmark and succeeds ("Strict bookmark subscribe failed, retrying without bookmark" → "Pull-mode subscription created successfully", 07:26:51). The identical recovery also fired on the Directory Service channel at the same startup.
- **During PULL (~2h later, while reading) → DOES NOT RECOVER.** At 09:36:09 the busy Security log rolled over past the open subscription; the pull path hit STALE and never re-subscribed — it backed off and retried the same dead subscription, still looping 17 min later (09:53:52). 436 STALE errors; ingestion stopped until restart.

Same channel, same error, opposite results → the problem is the **code path**, not the channel.

## Why only the Security channel stalls
Every channel uses the subscribe path at start and recovers. The pull-path STALE is only *triggered* on a channel busy enough to roll its log over while Vector is mid-read — Security, by far the highest-volume channel here. Quiet channels (Directory Service, etc.) never reach it. The failure tracks event volume, consistent with a log-rollover trigger.

## Root cause (v0.57.0 source)
In `src/sources/windows_event_log/subscription.rs`, inside the EvtNext drain loop:
- `ERROR_EVT_QUERY_RESULT_INVALID_POSITION` → calls `resubscribe_channel()` (subscription.rs:584-614)
- `ERROR_EVT_QUERY_RESULT_STALE` → only `channel_drained = true; break;`, no re-subscription (subscription.rs:574-583)

`resubscribe_channel()` (subscription.rs:806-895) already does the right thing: `EvtClose` the stale handle, `EvtSubscribe` again from the bookmark, and if the bookmark is itself stale, fall back to a bookmark-less subscription. The STALE branch never calls it. After the `break`, the pull loop in `mod.rs` (loop at mod.rs:389) backs off (100 ms → cap 5 s) and calls `EvtNext` on the **same** stale handle, which keeps returning STALE. The "speculative timeout" idle-cycle pull (mod.rs:496-524, from the lost-wakeup fix #25194/#25195) reuses the same stale handle too, so it cannot rescue a STALE subscription.

0.57.0's subscribe-time fallback (subscription.rs:269-314) runs only when a subscription is **opened** (start/restart, or inside `resubscribe_channel`) — never from the pull path. So STALE-while-reading recovers only via a restart. Same handling on 0.56.0, 0.57.0 and `master`.

## What Microsoft says
Per WinError.h, `ERROR_EVT_QUERY_RESULT_STALE` (Win32 15011 / HRESULT 0x80073AA3): *"The query result is not valid. This may be due to the log being cleared or rolling over after the query result was created. Release the query result object and reissue the query."* (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/wes/windows-event-log-error-constants). Under `EvtSubscribeStrict` the same error means "event records are missing" (EVT_SUBSCRIBE_CALLBACK). Microsoft's prescribed recovery is exactly release + reissue (= re-subscribe) — which the pull path fails to do.

## Expected behavior
On STALE, release the stale result and re-subscribe (as already done for `INVALID_POSITION`), falling back to oldest available if the bookmark is gone — so the source self-recovers at runtime, with no restart and no operator intervention.

## Actual behavior
No re-subscription on STALE; the source retries the invalidated handle forever and the channel stops ingesting until Vector is restarted.

## Suggested fix
In the STALE arm (subscription.rs:574-583), call the existing `resubscribe_channel()` — exactly as the `INVALID_POSITION` arm (subscription.rs:584-614) already does — instead of `break`ing. A few lines, reusing code that already handles the bookmark-stale fallback; matches Microsoft's documented remedy.


### Configuration

```text
sources:
  wineventlog_security:
    type: windows_event_log
    channels: ["Security"]
    read_existing_events: false
    # batch_size (100), event_timeout_ms (5000), events_per_second (0) all left at defaults
```

### Version

vector 0.57.0 (x86_64-pc-windows-msvc 8832452 2026-07-14) — also reproduced on 0.56.0; same pull-loop handling on master.

### Debug Output

```text
Relevant internal_logs lines (verbatim; only the host value redacted). Same 0.57.0 run.

WORKS — STALE at SUBSCRIBE recovers (Security, process start):
{"channel":"Security","error":"The query result is stale or invalid and must be recreated. This may be due to the log being cleared or rolling over after the query result was created. {"backoff_ms":5000,"error":"Failed to pull events from channel 'Security': The query result is stale or invalid and must be recreated. This may be due to the log being cleared or rolling over after the query result was created. (0x80073AA3)","host":"REDACTED","message":"Recoverable pull error, backing off.","metadata":{"kind":"event","level":"WARN","module_path":"vector::sources::windows_event_log","target":"vector::sources::windows_event_log"},"pid":4720,"source_type":"internal_logs","timestamp":"2026-08-14T09:53:52.434609200Z","vector":{"component_id":"wineventlog_security","component_kind":"source","component_type":"windows_event_log"}}

Separate, self-recovered lost wakeup on Directory Service at the same instant (not a STALE):
```

### Example Data

N/A — subscription-recovery bug, not a data/format issue.

### Additional Context

- Runs as a Windows service on a Domain Controller; ~9 windows_event_log channels as independent source instances (Application, System, Security, Directory Service, DFS Replication, DNS Server/Audit, among others) plus a file source and a scheduled exec source, all feeding one sink. No Kubernetes, no unusual CLI flags/env vars.
- Timeline: Security collected normally ~2h09m (07:27 → 09:36:09 UTC), then STALE; 436 STALE pull errors; ingestion stopped until restart. Same on 0.56.0 (~36,000 STALE errors over ~2 days, multi-hour Security gaps) — not specific to one build.


### References

- elastic/beats#45750 — "Winlog Beat does not recover from recoverable error when reading from Windows Event Log" (closed). Same STALE message; repro forces it with a small log max size so the log rolls over before events are read.
- vectordotdev/vector#25194 / #25195 — related lost-wakeup fix in the same source (different code path; does not cover this STALE pull case).

### Use Cases

If structured logs are used downstream (for statistics or investigating which events took place), it would be nice to be able to rely a bit more on the correct delivery of those logs. Currently, vector only has "best effort" for `docker_logs`, and if I read the docs/source correctly, it always reads the logs from the "now" (at the start) timestamp, and not from the start of the container or indeed from any kind of checkpoint. That means the "best effort" is a quite poor effort, where logs _will_ be lost if vector is restarted. This has kept me from using Vector (other tools like promtail or filebeat do checkpointing - don't know if they integrate that with acknowledgements though).

### Attempted Solutions

_No response_

### Proposal

- Introduce checkpointing to the `docker_logs` source, similar to the file source.
- Optionally integrate checkpointing with acknowledgements

I see that checkpointing hasn't been enough to upgrade the file source from best-effort to at-least-once delivery, which I assume is due to lack of acknowledgement integration. However, checkpoints is still a big upgrade to the reliability of the source, even without acknowledgement integration. But I do think both together would be enough to "upgrade" the classification.

### Use Cases

Hello,
In my environment, I constantly need to process large volumes of logs, and I'm focusing on structuring them.

In my current environment, I've implemented a lot of ingest pipelines using the common Elasticsearch and Filebeat, but I can't perform unit testing. Updating GROK patterns is a big mental burden.

Meanwhile, I discovered that Vector allows you to write tests in configuration files, which might allow for TDD (Test-Driven Development), so I gave it a try.

As you know, IP address information is very common in logs. Therefore, when using logs as a SIEM, the ASN, organization information, and CIDR information associated with IP addresses are very useful for aggregating and displaying information.
This allows you to group vast amounts of IP address data by CIDR and organization, which is convenient when displaying them in graphs or when viewing logs for specific CIDRs for security purposes, eliminating the need to specify each IP address one by one.
Pre-processing using a log ingestion agent is extremely beneficial because it reduces the barriers to analysis tools.

### Attempted Solutions

I noticed that some fields were missing when using Vector to perform the substitution performed by Elasticsearch's [GeoIP processor](https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/enrich-processor/geoip-processor).

https://github.com/vectordotdev/vector/blob/3749b70194de509fd0e12534f8affa35c490587b/src/enrichment_tables/geoip.rs#L175-L245

I noticed that a few fields were missing when using Vector to replace what Elasticsearch's [GeoIP processor](https://www.elastic.co/docs/reference/enrich-processor/geoip-processor) does.

The `network` field is the one that returns the CIDR in the database from the input IP address. Using this provides information that can be grouped, such as 192.0.2.0/24.

According to the documentation, the following databases support this network field:

* [GeoIP and GeoLite City and Country Databases](https://dev.maxmind.com/geoip/docs/databases/city-and-country/)
* [GeoIP Anonymous IP Databases](https://dev.maxmind.com/geoip/docs/databases/anonymous-ip/)
* [GeoIP ISP Databases](https://dev.maxmind.com/geoip/docs/databases/isp/)
* [GeoIP Connection Type Databases](https://dev.maxmind.com/geoip/docs/databases/connection-type/)
* [GeoLite ASN Database](https://dev.maxmind.com/geoip/docs/databases/asn/)

title: Decide on initial source
body:
Should we limit ourselves to places they've already deployed Filebeat, or do we need to support input from Splunk?

## Filebeat

If we're willing to tie ourselves to their Filebeat rollout, we have a few options:

* Lumberjack protocol (i.e. pretend to be Logstash)
* Kafka protocol
* Redis protocol

The Lumberjack protocol would take some research and reverse-engineering, since it is not directly documented. On the plus side, being a drop-in replacement for Logstash (at least for this type of input) could be interesting.

The Kafka protocol is not incredibly simple, but it's more of a known quantity and well designed for the type of workload we're targeting. It also has the big advantage of cluster-aware clients. Even though we're unlikely to support clustering right away, using the Kafka protocol gives us one of the only clear paths towards it.

The Redis protocol is very simple and would likely be the quickest way to get started.

## Splunk

If we're not willing to limit ourselves to places they've already rolled out alternatives to the Splunk collector, our only option (other than reverse-engineering the Splunk protocol, which is likely not allowed) is to implement a BSD syslog server.

The syslog protocol is quite simple and likely wouldn't take terribly long to implement, but it's not a protocol that provides the kind of features we want moving forward.
